belief.answer:
Put N=binom(n,2), H=(n^(n−2))!, B=2^(N+n), and δ(x)=floor(1/(|x|+1)). For 0≤b<2^N, let A_b be the symmetric zero-diagonal matrix whose upper-triangular entries, in lexicographic order, are the binary digits of b starting with the least significant digit. Set d_(b,i)=Σ_j(A_b)_(ij) and L_b=diag(d_(b,1),…,d_(b,n))−A_b. Write L_b^[S] for deletion of the rows and columns in S, and define a_b=det(L_b^[{n}]), f_(b,uv)=det(L_b^[{u,v}]), q_b=a_b+δ(a_b), and w_b=(1−δ(a_b))∏_(i=2)^n δ(d_(b,i)−d_(b,1)). Then, throughout the stated domain,
\[\boxed{\displaystyle t_n=\frac1H\left\lfloor\log_B\!\left(1+\sum_{b=0}^{2^N-1}w_b\sum_{1\le u<v\le n}B^{\,Hn d_{b,1}f_{b,uv}/q_b}\right)\right\rfloor.}\]

judge.answer: Put N=\binom n2, H=(n^{n-2})!, B=2^{N+n}, and δ(x)=\lfloor1/(|x|+1)\rfloor. For 0≤b<2^N, let A_b be the symmetric zero-diagonal matrix whose upper-triangular entries, in lexicographic order, are the binary digits of b starting with the least significant digit. Set d_{b,i}=\sum_j(A_b)_{ij} and L_b=\operatorname{diag}(d_{b,1},\ldots,d_{b,n})-A_b. Write L_b^{[S]} for deletion of the rows and columns in S, and define a_b=\det(L_b^{[\{n\}]}), f_{b,uv}=\det(L_b^{[\{u,v\}]}), q_b=a_b+δ(a_b), and w_b=(1-δ(a_b))\prod_{i=2}^n δ(d_{b,i}-d_{b,1}). Then, throughout the stated domain, \[\boxed{t_n=\frac1H\left\lfloor\log_B\!\left(1+\sum_{b=0}^{2^N-1}w_b\sum_{1\le u<v\le n}B^{Hn d_{b,1}f_{b,uv}/q_b}\right)\right\rfloor.}\]
judge.reason: It asserts an explicit exact formula for t_n, so it makes a provable claim. Its exhaustive graph-enumeration formula is a different claim from the residue-class formula in e1, not an equivalent rewriting of it.
judge.gate: The formula exhaustively enumerates all labeled graphs, filters for connected regular ones, computes their pairwise commute times via determinants, and encodes the maximum using a logarithm. It therefore repackages the defining optimization as a finite calculation rather than providing the explicit exact formula for t_n that the problem requests.

options.counterfactual: For infinitely many admissible even values of n, no cubic graph attains t_n; a regular graph of higher degree has a larger maximum commute time.
options.approach: Compare explicit constructions in degrees 3, 4, 5, and 6, maximizing degree times effective resistance rather than effective resistance alone. The commute-time identity makes this the relevant comparison at fixed n.

options.approach: Enumerate exact boundary resistance profiles for small replacements of several consecutive blocks. Compare the resulting rational resistances exactly, including replacements that appear numerically tied.
